title: p-Block Elements: Groups 15 to 18 (Nitrogen, Oxygen, Halogen & Noble Gas Families)
syllabus: Group 15 (Nitrogen family: N, P, As, Sb, Bi): Electronic configuration, trends in atomic/ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electronegativity; Oxidation states (-3, +3, +5), inert pair effect and stability of Bi(V) vs Bi(III); Anomalous behavior of nitrogen, catenation, dπ-pπ vs pπ-pπ bonding; Hydrides (thermal stability, reducing character, basicity, bond angle: NH3 > PH3 > AsH3 > SbH3 > BiH3); Oxides and oxoacids of nitrogen and phosphorus (structures, oxidation states, P-H reducing bonds); Allotropes of phosphorus (white, red, black). Group 16 (Chalcogens: O, S, Se, Te, Po): Electronic configurations, oxidation states (-2, +2, +4, +6); Hydrides (volatility, acidic strength, thermal stability: H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te); Allotropy of sulfur (rhombic, monoclinic, plastic), crown S8 ring, chair S6 ring, S2 paramagnetism in vapor state; Oxoacids of sulfur (structures, peroxo and thiono linkages, Caro's and Marshall's acids); Ozone (preparation, structure, oxidizing properties). Group 17 (Halogens: F, Cl, Br, I, At): Electronic configurations, oxidation states (-1 to +7); Anomalous behavior of fluorine (low bond dissociation energy of F2, hydrogen bonding); Oxidizing power trends (F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2); Hydracids (acidic strength: HF < HCl < HBr < HI; thermal stability and reducing power); Interhalogen compounds (types: XX', XX'3, XX'5, XX'7; shapes and reactivity); Oxoacids of halogens (acidic strength: HClO < HClO2 < HClO3 < HClO4). Group 18 (Noble Gases: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn): Electronic configuration, physical properties, inertness; Bartlett's discovery of xenon compounds; Xenon fluorides and oxides (XeF2, XeF4, XeF6, XeOF4, XeO3: preparation, hydrolysis, structures and VSEPR geometries); Uses of noble gases.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following arrangements represents the correct decreasing order of reducing character for the hydrides of Group 15?
questions.solution:
1. Down Group 15, the central atom size increases systematically from $\text{N}$ to $\text{Bi}$.
2. Consequently, the $\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond length increases and the bond dissociation enthalpy drops sharply ($\text{N}-\text{H} > \text{P}-\text{H} > \text{As}-\text{H} > \text{Sb}-\text{H} > \text{Bi}-\text{H}$).
3. Because the $\text{Bi}-\text{H}$ bond is the weakest and cleaves most readily to release hydrogen, **$\text{BiH}_3$ is the strongest reducing agent**.
4. $\text{NH}_3$ is a very mild reducing agent. Therefore, the decreasing order of reducing power is:
$$\text{BiH}_3 > \text{SbH}_3 > \text{AsH}_3 > \text{PH}_3 > \text{NH}_3$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In the vapor phase at elevated temperatures around $1000\text{ K}$, sulfur exhibits PARAMAGNETISM. This behavior is due to the presence of:
options: Two unpaired electrons in the $\pi^*$ antibonding orbitals of diatomic $\text{S}_2$ molecules
Unpaired electrons in the $3d$ subshell of $\text{S}_8$ rings
Homolytic cleavage of the puckered $\text{S}_6$ ring into diradicals
Single unpaired electron in the $\sigma_{3s}$ orbital
questions.solution:
1. In the vapor state at high temperatures ($T \sim 1000\text{ K}$), sulfur exists primarily as diatomic **$\text{S}_2$ molecules**.
2. Like molecular oxygen ($\text{O}_2$), $\text{S}_2$ has $12$ valence electrons ($16$ total for $\text{O}_2$, $32$ total for $\text{S}_2$).
3. In its ground-state molecular orbital configuration, the two highest-energy valence electrons occupy the degenerate **$\pi^*_{3p_x}$ and $\pi^*_{3p_y}$ antibonding orbitals singly with parallel spins** (by Hund's rule).
4. The presence of these two unpaired electrons makes vapor-phase $\text{S}_2$ **paramagnetic**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Complete hydrolysis of xenon hexafluoride ($\text{XeF}_6$) produces a colorless explosive solid $X$. Compound $X$ and its molecular geometry are respectively:
questions.solution:
1. Partial hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_6$ yields oxyfluorides:
   $$\text{XeF}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeOF}_4 + 2\text{HF}$$
   $$\text{XeF}_6 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2 + 4\text{HF}$$
2. **Complete hydrolysis** replaces all six fluorines with three oxygens to give xenon trioxide:
   $$\text{XeF}_6 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{XeO}_3 + 6\text{HF}$$
3. In $\text{XeO}_3$, xenon forms three $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bonds and retains one lone pair ($3\ \sigma\text{-bonds} + 1\text{ lp} = 4 \implies sp^3$ hybridization).
4. VSEPR geometry: **Trigonal pyramidal** (it is a colorless, highly explosive hygroscopic solid).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following oxoacids of phosphorus acts as a powerful REDUCING AGENT due to the presence of directly bonded hydrogen to phosphorus?
questions.solution:
1. In oxoacids of phosphorus, the reducing character is imparted exclusively by hydrogen atoms bonded directly to phosphorus ($\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds); hydrogens in $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ groups are ionizable as protons and do not act as reducing agents.
2. In hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$), the structure contains **two $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds**, one $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bond, and one $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bond.
3. Because it possesses the maximum number of $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds among phosphorus oxoacids, **$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ is a potent reducing agent** (e.g., reducing $\text{AgNO}_3$ to metallic silver):
   $$4\text{AgNO}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_2 \rightarrow 4\text{Ag} \downarrow + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 4\text{HNO}_3$$
4. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ has zero $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds and has no reducing capability.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] The correct increasing order of acidic strength for the oxoacids of chlorine is:
questions.solution:
1. In the series of chlorine oxoacids:
   - $\text{HClO}$: Hypochlorous acid ($\text{Cl}$ in $+1$ state)
   - $\text{HClO}_2$: Chlorous acid ($\text{Cl}$ in $+3$ state)
   - $\text{HClO}_3$: Chloric acid ($\text{Cl}$ in $+5$ state)
   - $\text{HClO}_4$: Perchloric acid ($\text{Cl}$ in $+7$ state)
2. As the oxidation state of chlorine increases, the electron-withdrawing inductive effect on the $\text{O}-\text{H}$ bond increases, weakening it and releasing $\text{H}^+$ more readily.
3. Furthermore, the conjugate bases ($\text{ClO}^-, \text{ClO}_2^-, \text{ClO}_3^-, \text{ClO}_4^-$) gain resonance stabilization as the number of terminal oxygen atoms increases; in the perchlorate ion ($\text{ClO}_4^-$), the negative charge is delocalized over four equivalent oxygen atoms.
4. Therefore, acidic strength increases as: $\text{HClO} < \text{HClO}_2 < \text{HClO}_3 < \text{HClO}_4$.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Why is bismuth in the $+5$ oxidation state (such as $\text{BiF}_5$ or $\text{NaBiO}_3$) a POWERFUL OXIDIZING AGENT?
options: Due to the inert pair effect, the $+3$ oxidation state of bismuth is far more stable than the $+5$ oxidation state
Because bismuth has the highest electronegativity in Group 15
Because $\text{Bi}^{5+}$ has a smaller ionic radius than $\text{Bi}^{3+}$
questions.solution:
1. In bismuth ($Z = 83$, $[\text{Xe}] 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^2 6p^3$), the intervening $4f^{14}$ and $5d^{10}$ subshells provide poor shielding for the valence $6s^2$ electrons.
2. The high effective nuclear charge binds the $6s^2$ electron pair tightly to the nucleus, making it reluctant to unpair and participate in bonding (**inert pair effect**).
3. Consequently, the **$+3$ oxidation state is far more stable than the $+5$ state** for bismuth ($\text{Bi}^{3+} \gg \text{Bi}^{5+}$).
4. When forced into the $+5$ state (as in bismuthate, $\text{BiO}_3^-$), bismuth readily accepts two electrons to be reduced to stable $\text{Bi}^{3+}$, acting as an exceptionally **powerful oxidizing agent**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Neil Bartlett was inspired to prepare the first noble gas compound, $\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$, based on the observation that:
options: The first ionization enthalpy of molecular oxygen ($1175\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) is almost identical to that of xenon ($1170\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$)
Xenon reacts spontaneously with oxygen gas at room temperature
Platinum hexafluoride is a strong reducing agent
Helium forms stable clathrates with water
questions.solution:
1. In 1962, Neil Bartlett prepared the red ionic compound dioxygenyl hexafluoroplatinate, $\text{O}_2^+ [\text{PtF}_6]^-$, by oxidizing molecular oxygen with $\text{PtF}_6$.
2. He realized that the first ionization enthalpy of molecular oxygen ($1175\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) was almost identical to the first ionization enthalpy of xenon gas ($1170\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), and both have comparable molecular/atomic dimensions.
3. He mixed xenon gas with deep red $\text{PtF}_6$ vapor at room temperature, which reacted immediately to precipitate the yellow-orange solid **$\text{Xe}^+[\text{PtF}_6]^-$**, disproving the long-held belief that noble gases are chemically inert.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Among the Group 16 hydrides $\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{H}_2\text{S}, \text{H}_2\text{Se},$ and $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, which one has the LOWEST boiling point?
questions.solution:
1. $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ exhibits extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, giving it an abnormally high boiling point ($373\text{ K}$) despite its small molar mass.
2. From $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, hydrogen bonding is negligible; boiling points are governed by molecular mass and polarizability (London dispersion forces).
3. As molecular weight increases from $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ to $\text{H}_2\text{Te}$, dispersion forces strengthen, and boiling points rise: $\text{H}_2\text{S} (213\text{ K}) < \text{H}_2\text{Se} (232\text{ K}) < \text{H}_2\text{Te} (269\text{ K})$.
4. Therefore, **$\text{H}_2\text{S}$ has the lowest boiling point** in the entire group.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In white phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$), the number of $\text{P}-\text{P}$ single covalent bonds, the bond angle, and the hybridization of phosphorus atoms are respectively:
questions.solution:
1. White phosphorus exists as discrete tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ molecules.
2. Each phosphorus atom is at a vertex of the tetrahedron, bonded to three other phosphorus atoms along the six edges:
   $$\text{Number of } \text{P}-\text{P}\text{ bonds} = 6$$
3. The tetrahedral apex geometry forces the $\text{P}-\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond angle to be **$60^\circ$**.
4. Because the $sp^3$-hybridized phosphorus atoms normally prefer $109.5^\circ$, the $60^\circ$ angle introduces severe **angular ring strain**.
5. This structural strain makes white phosphorus highly reactive, unstable, and spontaneously flammable in air (chemiluminescent).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] What is the correct order of bond dissociation enthalpy for the halogen molecules?
questions.solution:
1. Normally, bond dissociation enthalpy decreases as halogen atoms become larger down Group 17.
2. However, **$\text{F}_2$ has an anomalously low bond dissociation energy** ($158.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$), lower than both $\text{Cl}_2$ ($242.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) and $\text{Br}_2$ ($192.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).
3. In $\text{F}_2$, the $\text{F}-\text{F}$ bond distance is very short ($142\text{ pm}$); the compact, non-bonding electron lone pairs on adjacent fluorine atoms experience intense electrostatic repulsions, weakening the single bond.
4. Therefore, the actual order of bond dissociation enthalpy is:
$$\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{F}_2 > \text{I}_2$$

questions.question: [NEET 2021] In Marshall's acid (peroxodisulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$) and Caro's acid (peroxomonosulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$), the oxidation state of sulfur is:
options: $+7$ in Marshall's acid and $+8$ in Caro's acid
$+6$ in Marshall's acid and $+4$ in Caro's acid
questions.solution:
1. In Caro's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$): Structure is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{H}$. It contains one peroxo linkage (two oxygen atoms at $-1$) and three oxo/hydroxyl oxygens at $-2$:
   $$2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies x = +6$$
2. In Marshall's acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$): Structure is $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$. It contains one central peroxo bridge ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$) and six non-peroxo oxygens:
   $$2(+1) + 2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = +6$$
Both acids contain sulfur in its maximum stable group oxidation state of **$+6$**.

questions.question: Interhalogen compounds are generally MORE REACTIVE than pure homonuclear halogens (with the exception of $\text{F}_2$). This is because:
options: The $\text{X}-\text{X}'$ bond in interhalogens is polar and weaker than the non-polar $\text{X}-\text{X}$ bond in elemental halogens
The electronegativity difference makes them non-polar
questions.solution:
1. In an interhalogen molecule $\text{X}-\text{X}'$, the two halogen atoms differ in electronegativity and covalent radius.
2. The overlap between two different halogen orbitals is less effective than in symmetric homonuclear bonds, making the heteronuclear **$\text{X}-\text{X}'$ bond weaker and more polar** than the homonuclear $\text{X}-\text{X}$ bond.
3. Consequently, the activation energy for bond cleavage is lower, rendering interhalogens **more chemically reactive** than pure halogens (except $\text{F}_2$, whose bond is weakened by lone pair repulsions).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] In the brown ring test for the detection of nitrate ions ($\text{NO}_3^-$), the brown ring formed at the junction of the two liquids has the chemical formula:
questions.solution:
1. Nitrate ions are reduced by freshly prepared $\text{FeSO}_4$ in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$):
   $$\text{NO}_3^- + 3\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NO} + 3\text{Fe}^{3+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. The nitric oxide coordinates with unreacted hydrated ferrous ions to form the brown pentaaquanitrosyliron complex:
   $$[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+} + \text{NO} \rightarrow [\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. The coordination compound is **$[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]\text{SO}_4$** (where $\text{NO}$ acts as a $+1$ nitrosonium ligand and iron is in the $+1$ oxidation state, $d^7$ with $3$ unpaired electrons).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Which of the following noble gases is used in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) systems and cryogenic research to maintain superconducting magnets at liquid temperatures?
questions.solution:
1. **Liquid Helium** has the lowest boiling point of any known substance ($4.2\text{ K}$ or $-268.9^\circ\text{C}$).
2. Because it remains liquid near absolute zero, it is the premier **cryogenic refrigerant** used to cool the superconducting electromagnets in clinical Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners and NMR spectrometers.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] The basicity (number of ionizable protons) of pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$) is:
questions.solution:
1. Pyrophosphoric acid (diphosphoric acid) is obtained by heating orthophosphoric acid:
   $$2\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. Its structure contains two phosphoryl groups linked via a bridging oxygen: $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$.
3. The molecule has **four $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ groups** and zero $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds.
4. All four hydrogen atoms attached to electronegative oxygen atoms are ionizable as protons, making pyrophosphoric acid a **tetrabasic acid (basicity = $4$)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What is the hybridization and shape of the interhalogen molecule iodine heptafluoride ($\text{IF}_7$)?
questions.solution:
1. In $\text{IF}_7$, the central iodine atom has $7$ valence electrons.
2. It forms seven single $\text{I}-\text{F}$ covalent bonds with seven fluorine atoms, leaving zero lone pairs.
3. $\text{Steric Number} = 7\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} = 7 \implies \mathbf{sp^3d^3}$ hybridization.
4. To minimize steric repulsion, the five equatorial $\text{I}-\text{F}$ bonds lie in a plane at $72^\circ$ angles, while two axial bonds lie along the perpendicular axis at $90^\circ$.
5. Therefore, the geometry is **Pentagonal bipyramidal**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following statements about ozone ($\text{O}_3$) is INCORRECT?
options: The two $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond lengths in ozone are different, one being a true single bond and the other a true double bond
Ozone is a bent molecule with a bond angle of about $117^\circ$
Ozone acts as a powerful oxidizing agent because it easily decomposes to liberate nascent oxygen
Ozone is thermodynamically unstable relative to oxygen because its decomposition has $\Delta H < 0$ and $\Delta S > 0$
questions.solution:
1. Ozone is a resonance hybrid of two equivalent canonical Lewis structures: $\text{O}=\text{O}^+-\text{O}^- \longleftrightarrow ^-\text{O}-\text{O}^+=\text{O}$.
2. Because of resonance delocalization, the two $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bonds are **identical in length ($128\text{ pm}$)**, intermediate between a single bond ($148\text{ pm}$) and a double bond ($121\text{ pm}$).
3. Ozone has a bent shape with a bond angle of $116.8^\circ \approx 117^\circ$.
4. It decomposes via $2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{O}_2$ with negative $\Delta H$ and positive $\Delta S$ (large negative $\Delta G$), making it thermodynamically unstable and explosive at high concentrations.
Therefore, Statement A is incorrect.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] When chlorine gas reacts with COLD, DILUTE sodium hydroxide solution, the chlorine-containing products formed are:
questions.solution:
Chlorine undergoes disproportionation with aqueous alkali depending on temperature and concentration:
1. With **cold and dilute $\text{NaOH}$**:
   $$2\text{NaOH}(\text{cold, dil.}) + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{NaOCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
   Products: Chloride ($\text{Cl}^-$, $-1$) and Hypochlorite ($\text{OCl}^-$, $+1$).
2. With **hot and concentrated $\text{NaOH}$**:
   $$6\text{NaOH}(\text{hot, conc.}) + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 5\text{NaCl} + \text{NaClO}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
   Products: Chloride ($-1$) and Chlorate ($+5$).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following compounds has a SEE-SAW geometry according to VSEPR theory?
questions.solution:
1. In sulfur tetrafluoride ($\text{SF}_4$):
- Central sulfur has $6$ valence electrons.
- Forms $4$ single bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving $1$ lone pair ($4\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} = 5$).
- $\text{Steric Number} = 5 \implies sp^3d$ hybridization.
- The lone pair occupies an equatorial position, giving a **See-saw** shape.
2. $\text{XeF}_4$ has $4\text{ bp} + 2\text{ lp} = 6 \implies$ Square planar.
3. $\text{CCl}_4$ and $\text{SiF}_4$ have $4\text{ bp} + 0\text{ lp} = 4 \implies$ Tetrahedral.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) in the solid state exists as an ionic crystal consisting of:
questions.solution:
1. In the gas phase, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is a covalent molecule with an oxygen bridge: $\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{O}-\text{NO}_2$.
2. In the **solid crystalline state**, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ completely ionizes into a salt:
   $$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(s) \equiv [\text{NO}_2]^+ [\text{NO}_3]^- \quad (\text{Nitronium nitrate})$$
3. Geometry of the ions:
   - **Nitronium cation ($[\text{NO}_2]^+$):** $2\ \sigma\text{-bonds} + 0\text{ lp} \implies sp$ hybridized, **Linear** ($180^\circ$).
   - **Nitrate anion ($[\text{NO}_3]^-$):** $3\ \sigma\text{-bonds} + 0\text{ lp} \implies sp^2$ hybridized, **Trigonal planar** ($120^\circ$).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$) produces smoke rings (Vortex rings) when bubbled through water into air. This spontaneous flammability is due to the presence of traces of:
questions.solution:
1. Pure phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$) is non-inflammable at room temperature.
2. However, when prepared by the reaction of white phosphorus with caustic soda, it contains volatile impurities of **diphosphine ($\text{P}_2\text{H}_4$) or $\text{P}_4$ vapor**.
3. $\text{P}_2\text{H}_4$ is spontaneously flammable in contact with atmospheric oxygen, igniting the $\text{PH}_3$ and producing vortex rings of white $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ smoke (used in Holmes signals).

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Bleaching action of sulfur dioxide ($\text{SO}_2$) is TEMPORARY, whereas the bleaching action of chlorine ($\text{Cl}_2$) is PERMANENT. This is because:
options: $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by reduction (which is reversed by atmospheric oxygen), while $\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by oxidation
$\text{Cl}_2$ bleaches by reduction, while $\text{SO}_2$ bleaches by oxidation
$\text{SO}_2$ is an acidic gas, while $\text{Cl}_2$ is neutral
questions.solution:
1. In moisture, sulfur dioxide acts as a **reducing agent** by releasing nascent hydrogen:
   $$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2[\text{H}]$$
   The colored matter is reduced to a colorless compound. Upon standing in air, atmospheric oxygen oxidizes it back to its colored form (temporary bleaching).
2. Chlorine in water releases nascent oxygen (**oxidation**):
   $$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HCl} + [\text{O}]$$
   $$\text{Colored matter} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{Colorless oxidized product}$$
   Oxidative bleaching irreversibly destroys the chromophore, making it permanent.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following noble gases does NOT form clathrate compounds with quinol or water because of its small atomic size?
questions.solution:
1. **Clathrate compounds** (cage inclusion complexes) are formed when guest noble gas atoms become physically trapped inside cavities within the hydrogen-bonded host crystal lattices of hydroquinone or ice.
2. **Helium and Neon** have tiny atomic diameters ($0.98\text{ \AA}$ and $1.60\text{ \AA}$).
3. Because they are smaller than the openings of the cage cavities, they easily slip out through the lattice channels without being held.
4. Therefore, Helium and Neon do not form stable clathrate compounds, whereas $\text{Ar}, \text{Kr},$ and $\text{Xe}$ form them readily.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The correct order of bond angles in the hydrides $\text{NH}_3, \text{PH}_3, \text{AsH}_3,$ and $\text{SbH}_3$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Down Group 15, the electronegativity of the central atom decreases markedly ($\text{N} = 3.0 > \text{P} = 2.1 > \text{As} = 2.0 > \text{Sb} = 1.9$).
2. In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen pulls the bond-pair electrons close to itself, producing strong bond pair-bond pair electrostatic repulsion that keeps the bond angle wide ($107.8^\circ$).
3. In heavier hydrides ($\text{PH}_3, \text{AsH}_3, \text{SbH}_3$), bonding involves almost pure, unhybridized $p$-orbitals (Drago's rule), causing the bond pairs to lie further out and bond angles to approach $90^\circ$:
$$\text{NH}_3 (107.8^\circ) > \text{PH}_3 (93.6^\circ) > \text{AsH}_3 (91.8^\circ) > \text{SbH}_3 (91.3^\circ)$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] What is the total number of lone pairs of electrons in a molecule of xenon difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$)?
questions.solution:
1. In $\text{XeF}_2$:
- The central xenon atom has $8$ valence electrons, forms $2$ single bonds with fluorine atoms, and retains $6$ non-bonding electrons $\implies$ **$3$ lone pairs on $\text{Xe}$**.
- Each terminal fluorine atom has $7$ valence electrons, uses $1$ for bonding, and retains $6$ non-bonding electrons $\implies$ **$3$ lone pairs on each fluorine** ($2 \times 3 = 6$ lone pairs).
2. Total number of lone pairs in the entire molecule:
$$\text{Total lone pairs} = 3\text{ (on Xe)} + 6\text{ (on F)} = 9$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Concentrated nitric acid oxidizes red phosphorus to:
questions.solution:
1. Concentrated nitric acid is a powerful oxidizing agent.
2. When heated with elemental phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$), it oxidizes phosphorus to its highest stable oxidation state ($+5$), producing orthophosphoric acid along with reddish-brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas:
   $$\text{P}_4 + 20\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \xrightarrow{\Delta} 4\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 20\text{NO}_2 \uparrow + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2022] What is the basicity of phosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$)?
questions.solution:
1. The structural formula of phosphorous acid (orthophosphorous acid, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$) is:
   $$\text{H}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$$
2. It contains:
   - One $\text{P}=\text{O}$ double bond
   - One $\text{P}-\text{H}$ covalent bond (non-ionizable, responsible for reducing properties)
   - **Two $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bonds** (ionizable protons)
3. Because only the two hydrogens attached to oxygen can dissociate as $\text{H}^+$ ions in water, $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ is a **dibasic acid (basicity = $2$)**.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Rhombic sulfur and monoclinic sulfur are two allotropes of sulfur. The transition temperature at which both allotropes coexist in dynamic equilibrium at $1\text{ atm}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Below $369\text{ K}$, $\alpha$-rhombic sulfur (yellow octahedral crystals) is the stable allotrope.
2. Above $369\text{ K}$, $\beta$-monoclinic sulfur (needle-shaped crystals) is the stable allotrope.
3. At exactly **$369\text{ K}$ ($95.6^\circ\text{C} \approx 96^\circ\text{C}$)**, both forms coexist in equilibrium at $1\text{ atm}$. This temperature is termed the **transition temperature** (enantiotropy).

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following is the strongest oxidizing agent among the halogens in aqueous solution?
questions.solution:
The standard electrode potential ($E^\circ$) for the reduction $\frac{1}{2}\text{X}_2 + e^- \rightarrow \text{X}^-(aq)$ depends on three thermodynamic parameters:
1. Low bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{F}_2$ (requires little energy to dissociate)
2. High negative electron gain enthalpy
3. **Extremely high hydration enthalpy of the tiny $\text{F}^-$ ion**
Due to the massive release of hydration enthalpy, the reduction potential of fluorine is the highest ($E^\circ = +2.87\text{ V}$), making **$\text{F}_2$ the strongest oxidizing agent** in chemistry.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In which of the following reactions does dinitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) act as an inert gas under ordinary conditions?
options: It does not react at room temperature due to the very high bond dissociation energy of the $\text{N}\equiv\text{N}$ triple bond ($945.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$)
It forms protective nitride layers on all materials
It has a negative electron gain enthalpy
questions.solution:
1. The dinitrogen molecule contains an exceptionally strong triple bond ($:N \equiv N:$) between the two nitrogen atoms with a very short bond length ($109.8\text{ pm}$).
2. The bond dissociation enthalpy is enormous (**$945.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$**).
3. Consequently, dinitrogen is chemically inert and unreactive at ambient temperatures, requiring high temperatures or catalysts to react.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] When copper turnings are treated with DILUTE nitric acid and CONCENTRATED nitric acid, the gaseous products evolved respectively are:
questions.solution:
1. With **dilute nitric acid**, copper is oxidized to $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ while nitrate is reduced to colorless nitric oxide gas ($\text{NO}$):
   $$3\text{Cu} + 8\text{HNO}_3(\text{dil.}) \rightarrow 3\text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO} \uparrow + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
2. With **concentrated nitric acid**, copper yields dense reddish-brown nitrogen dioxide gas ($\text{NO}_2$):
   $$\text{Cu} + 4\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow \text{Cu}(\text{NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO}_2 \uparrow + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Therefore, the gases are $\text{NO}$ and $\text{NO}_2$ respectively.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] What is the shape and hybridization of the central atom in chlorine pentafluoride ($\text{ClF}_5$)?
questions.solution:
1. In $\text{ClF}_5$, the central chlorine atom has $7$ valence electrons.
2. Forms $5$ single bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving $1$ lone pair ($5\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} = 6$).
3. $\text{Steric Number} = 6 \implies \mathbf{sp^3d^2}$ hybridization (octahedral electron geometry).
4. With one position occupied by a lone pair, the molecular shape is **Square pyramidal**.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Oleum is commercially produced in the Contact process by absorbing sulfur trioxide in concentrated sulfuric acid. The chemical formula of oleum is:
questions.solution:
1. In the Contact process, $\text{SO}_3$ is not absorbed directly in water because it forms an unmanageable, corrosive acid mist.
2. Instead, $\text{SO}_3$ gas is absorbed in $98\%\ \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to produce fuming sulfuric acid (**oleum**):
   $$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$$
3. The product is **pyrosulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_7$)**, which is diluted with calculated amounts of water to obtain sulfuric acid of desired strength.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Aqua regia, which dissolves noble metals like gold and platinum, is a fresh mixture of concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ in the volumetric ratio of:
questions.solution:
1. **Aqua regia** ('royal water') is a freshly prepared mixture consisting of:
   $$\mathbf{3\text{ parts of concentrated } \text{HCl} + 1\text{ part of concentrated } \text{HNO}_3}$$
2. The mixture reacts to generate nascent chlorine and nitrosyl chloride:
   $$\text{HNO}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NOCl} + \text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
3. Nascent chlorine oxidizes gold and platinum into soluble chlorometallate complexes ($[\text{AuCl}_4]^-$ and $[\text{PtCl}_6]^{2-}$).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Which of the following xenon fluorides acts as a FLUORIDE ION ACCEPTOR when reacted with metal fluorides like $\text{KF}$?
questions.solution:
1. Xenon fluorides act as fluoride ion donors when reacted with strong fluoride acceptors like $\text{PF}_5, \text{SbF}_5,$ or $\text{AsF}_5$ (forming cations like $[\text{XeF}]^+$ and $[\text{XeF}_5]^+$).
2. However, **$\text{XeF}_6$ can also act as a fluoride ion acceptor** when reacted with alkali metal fluorides ($\text{MF}$, where $\text{M} = \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}, \text{Cs}$):
   $$\text{XeF}_6 + \text{MF} \rightarrow \text{M}^+ [\text{XeF}_7]^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{M}_2[\text{XeF}_8]$$
3. Therefore, $\text{XeF}_6$ forms heptafluoroxenate(VI) and octafluoroxenate(VI) complexes.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Nitrogen forms diatomic $\text{N}_2$ gas with a triple bond, whereas phosphorus forms tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ with single bonds. This is because:
options: Nitrogen has a small atomic size and forms strong $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds, whereas larger phosphorus atoms cannot effectively overlap sideways to form $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds
Phosphorus is more electronegative than nitrogen
questions.solution:
1. Nitrogen's small size ($r \approx 70\text{ pm}$) allows its $2p$ orbitals to approach close enough for strong, effective **lateral $p\pi-p\pi$ overlap**, producing a stable triple bond ($:N \equiv N:$).
2. Phosphorus has a much larger atomic radius ($r \approx 110\text{ pm}$), and its diffuse $3p$ orbitals cannot effectively overlap sideways.
3. A $\text{P}=\text{P}$ double bond is much weaker than two single $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bonds.
4. Therefore, phosphorus achieves thermodynamic stability by forming four tetrahedral vertices linked by **six single $\sigma$-bonds** in $\text{P}_4$.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following is the correct order of thermal stability for the hydracids of the halogens?
questions.solution:
1. Thermal stability of hydrogen halides depends directly on the bond dissociation enthalpy of the $\text{H}-\text{X}$ bond.
2. From $\text{F}$ to $\text{I}$, halogen size increases, bond length increases, and bond strength drops:
   - $\text{H}-\text{F}$: $567\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
   - $\text{H}-\text{Cl}$: $431\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
   - $\text{H}-\text{Br}$: $366\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
   - $\text{H}-\text{I}$: $299\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
3. Therefore, thermal stability decreases in the sequence:
$$\text{HF} > \text{HCl} > \text{HBr} > \text{HI}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2020] In the preparation of sulfuric acid by the Contact process, the catalyst used for the oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ is:
options: Finely divided iron with molybdenum promoter
questions.solution:
1. The key reversible step in the Contact process is:
   $$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g); \quad \Delta H = -196.6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
2. **Vanadium pentoxide ($\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$)** at $720\text{ K}$ and $2\text{ bar}$ pressure is the industrial catalyst used today (replacing platinized asbestos, which was easily poisoned by arsenic impurities).

questions.question: [NEET 2022] Why does fluorine exhibit ONLY a $-1$ oxidation state in its chemical compounds (apart from $0$ in $\text{F}_2$), whereas other halogens exhibit $+1, +3, +5,$ and $+7$ oxidation states?
options: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and lacks vacant $d$-orbitals in its valence shell
Fluorine has the lowest ionization enthalpy
Fluorine is a gas at room temperature
questions.solution:
1. Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of all elements ($4.0$ on the Pauling scale), so it always pulls shared electrons toward itself, precluding positive oxidation states.
2. Fluorine belongs to Period 2 ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^5$) and has **no vacant $d$-orbitals** in its valence shell ($n = 2$) to unpair and promote electrons for octet expansion.
3. Heavy halogens ($\text{Cl}, \text{Br}, \text{I}$) possess vacant $nd$-orbitals and lower electronegativities, allowing them to expand their valency to $+1, +3, +5,$ and $+7$ with oxygen and fluorine.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] The reaction of red hot carbon with concentrated nitric acid produces:
questions.solution:
1. Concentrated nitric acid is a powerful non-metal oxidizing agent.
2. When heated with carbon, it oxidizes carbon completely to carbon dioxide while being reduced to nitrogen dioxide:
   $$\text{C} + 4\text{HNO}_3(\text{conc.}) \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 \uparrow + 4\text{NO}_2 \uparrow + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

questions.question: [NEET 2023] The cyclic trimer of sulfur trioxide in the solid state, $(\text{SO}_3)_3$, has how many $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ bridge bonds?
questions.solution:
1. Solid sulfur trioxide exists as a cyclic trimer, $\gamma-\text{SO}_3$ (or $\text{S}_3\text{O}_9$).
2. Its structure consists of a puckered **six-membered ring containing alternating sulfur and oxygen atoms**:
   $$-[-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-\text{S}(=\text{O})_2-\text{O}-]-$$
3. The three sulfur atoms are linked together through three oxygen atoms, forming exactly **$3$ $\text{S}-\text{O}-\text{S}$ bridge bonds**.

questions.question: [NEET 2020] Helium is mixed with oxygen in the breathing gas cylinders used by deep-sea divers because:
options: Helium has very low solubility in blood at high pressures compared to nitrogen
Helium is lighter than air and allows faster swimming
Helium reacts chemically with carbon dioxide to purify alveolar air
questions.solution:
1. Atmospheric air contains $\sim 78\%\ \text{N}_2$. Under high hydrostatic pressures underwater, nitrogen dissolves in blood in large amounts.
2. During rapid ascent, the pressure drops quickly, and dissolved nitrogen comes out of solution as bubbles in capillaries and nerves, causing decompression sickness ('the bends').
3. Helium has very low polarizability and an exceptionally **low solubility in human blood** even at extreme pressures.
4. Therefore, diving gas mixtures (such as Trimix or Heliox: $11.7\%\ \text{He}, 56.2\%\ \text{N}_2, 32.1\%\ \text{O}_2$) substitute helium for nitrogen to prevent decompression sickness.

questions.question: [NEET 2022] In white phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$) and red phosphorus, the structures are respectively:
options: Discrete tetrahedral $\text{P}_4$ molecules and a polymeric chain of $\text{P}_4$ tetrahedra linked together
Polymeric sheet structure and discrete molecules
Both are giant network lattices like diamond
questions.solution:
1. **White phosphorus:** Consists of individual, discrete tetrahedral **$\text{P}_4$ molecules** held by weak van der Waals forces, making it soft, volatile, low-melting ($317\text{ K}$), and chemically reactive.
2. **Red phosphorus:** Formed by heating white phosphorus at $573\text{ K}$ in an inert atmosphere. One $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond in each tetrahedron opens up to link adjacent tetrahedra into a **polymeric chain of $\text{P}_4$ units**.
3. Because of this polymeric structure, red phosphorus is much less strained, denser, non-poisonous, and chemically more stable.

questions.question: [NEET 2021] Which of the following halogen oxides is used for the estimation of carbon monoxide in air samples?
questions.solution:
1. Diiodine pentoxide ($\text{I}_2\text{O}_5$) is an excellent oxidizing agent.
2. It oxidizes carbon monoxide quantitatively at room temperature to carbon dioxide, liberating elemental iodine:
   $$\text{I}_2\text{O}_5 + 5\text{CO} \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 5\text{CO}_2$$
3. The liberated iodine is titrated with standard sodium thiosulfate solution, providing a precise analytical method for determining toxic $\text{CO}$ concentrations in industrial and atmospheric air.

questions.question: [NEET 2023] Which of the following xenon compounds is ISOSTRUCTURAL with $\text{IF}_5$?
questions.solution:
1. For $\text{IF}_5$:
- Steric number $= 5\text{ bp} + 1\text{ lp} = 6 \implies sp^3d^2$ hybridization.
- VSEPR shape: **Square pyramidal**.
2. For $\text{XeOF}_4$:
- Xenon forms four single $\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ bonds, one $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ double bond, and retains one lone pair ($5\ \sigma\text{-bonds} + 1\text{ lp} = 6 \implies sp^3d^2$).
- VSEPR shape: **Square pyramidal**.
Because both species share identical $sp^3d^2$ hybridization, five surrounding bonding domains, and one axial lone pair, **$\text{XeOF}_4$ is isostructural with $\text{IF}_5$**.
